thread:
alisa-support: FYI escalated ticket from Acme, multiple 401s on signed requests after a deploy. They say it worked yesterday.

alisa-support: Error sample from our gateway logs: 
```
time=2026-03-16T22:41:02Z lvl=warn msg=auth.failed path=/v1/generate status=401 err="signature verification failed" kid=key-2026-03-16 client_id=acme-42
```

alisa-support: Customer sent a signed JWT they generate with their in-house SDK. They included header `alg: RSASSA-PSS` in the JWT. They say they haven't changed code.

matt-eng: Can you paste the full raw JWT (headers.payload.signature) redacting sensitive bits? I want to check the header fields and timestamps.

alisa-support: Pasted privately to the channel DM. Summary: header shows `alg: PS256`, `kid: acme-key-v2`, payload has `iat` and `exp` where `exp` looks like 13-digit ms epoch: `exp: 1710676862000`.

nora-sre: Interesting — our token time checks treat `exp` as seconds (10-digit). A 13-digit value would be way in the future -> should be accepted, not rejected. So maybe the failure is signature, not time.

jen-security: Happens to match a class of failures I saw once: client signs with RSASSA-PSS (PS256) but our gateway validator library historically only validated RS256 (PKCS1v1.5). If header says PS256 but validator interprets payload as RS256, verification fails with 'signature verification failed'. Do gateway logs show the exact alg we attempted to use?

api-gateway-bot: auth.verify_attempt: alg_attempt=RS256 alg_header=PS256 result=fail error="unsupported algorithm" node=gw-12

matt-eng: That bot log is golden. It looks like our validator attempted RS256 despite header=PS256. Why would that mapping happen? Any conditional fallbacks in the code?

jen-security: Possible root causes: (1) The JWKS entry for acme-key-v2 carries a `kty` or `alg` mismatch; (2) Our local jwks cache entry is stale and doesn't include the `pss` metadata so verifier uses default; (3) There's a bug in the header->verifier dispatcher where header alg with "PS256" collides with a normalization map that erroneously maps to RS256.

alisa-support: Customer confirms they rotated keys two days ago and we show a JWKS refresh 36h ago on their tenant. Could be stale. They also noted they upgraded openssl on their side recently.

nora-sre: Repro steps I ran locally: pulled the raw JWT, fetched JWKS from acme's issuer url, used `openssl pkey -pubin -in acme_v2_pub.pem -text` then verified signature with `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature sig.bin` using PSS params and it verifies fine. So the token is valid for PS256.

matt-eng: On our side, I instrumented the verifier to log algorithm dispatch: `alg_header=PS256 -> verifier=rsassa_pkcs1_v1_5` in a hot path. Added extra logging and a guard to reject when header alg != verifier.alg. Deploying a canary now to gw-12.

nora-sre: Also noticed cache timing: our jwks-cache TTL is 5m but we had a race where jwks-refresh disabled for 1h due to a transient upstream error; gw-12 still had old metadata for acme-key-v2 that lacked `use: "sig"` and alg info. That could force fallback behavior.

jen-security: Two-step root cause seems likely: client rotated keys and switched to PS256; our jwks cache was stale + dispatcher bug causing a default to RS256. Combined -> signature mismatch.

lewis-cs: Customer urgently needs this unblocked for live traffic. Any mitigation besides forcing them to revert to RS256?

matt-eng: Short-term mitigation: (1) Force gw-12 to purge jwks cache for acme tenant (I have a script). (2) Push a config change to treat absent alg metadata as 'trust header' for alg selection (stop mapping to RS256). That reduces risk but is less strict.

nora-sre: I just ran `curl -X POST https://gw-admin.internal/cache/purge -d '{"tenant":"acme-42","type":"jwks"}'` on gw-12 and gw-14. Responses OK. Monitoring logs now.

api-gateway-bot: cache.purge: tenant=acme-42 type=jwks status=ok nodes=[gw-12,gw-14] time=2026-03-16T22:43:15Z

matt-eng: Pushed the verifier guard to canary and enabled debug logging for alg dispatch. If this fixes it we should roll to prod.

alisa-support: Customer reports immediate drop in 401s, from ~120/min to <5/min. They're back online. :tada:

jen-security: Next actions: (1) hotfix to enforce header algorithm usage and fail closed if mismatch (don't silently map); (2) increase jwks cache TTL/better invalidate-on-rotation signals; (3) add telemetry for alg mismatches and jwks-cache-staleness events.

matt-eng: I opened a quick issue: ENGSEC-1872 - "alg dispatch fallback -> causes PS256-signed JWTs to fail when jwks missing alg metadata". Assigning to me for hotfix.

nora-sre: Postmortem note for runbook: when customer reports signature errors but tokens verify locally, check: 1) gateway alg_dispatch logs, 2) jwks cache age for tenant, 3) whether JWKS entry includes `alg`/`use`/`x5c` fields, 4) any CDN or proxy rewriting of `kid` header.

lewis-cs: Customer very thankful and asked for a short explanation they can paste into internal docs. I sent a summary.

jen-security: Follow-up: schedule a postmortem doc and consider adding automated detection that compares header.alg to jwks.alg and surfaces mismatch in console.

matt-eng: Marking thread resolved for now. Will update ENGSEC ticket with RCA and patch PR link.

alisa-support: Thanks all, closing the customer escalation.
